title: Parameter contracts and interop guidelines for function-calling (schema format & error taxonomy)
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary: Define a single, backwards-compatible JSON-schema-based parameter contract for function/tool calling across hosted, dedicated, and private runtimes. Goals are: (1) a compact authoring format that maps cleanly to OpenAPI/JSON Schema syntax used by clients, (2) clearly defined validation modes (strict, permissive, coercive) and defaults, (3) a consistent error taxonomy and user-facing error shapes with actionable suggestions, (4) compatibility rules for rolling changes and deprecation, and (5) telemetry hooks to classify validation failures by customer, route, and model variant.

Why: Current callers and servers disagree about typing (numbers vs strings), optional vs omitted fields, and how to report partial validation failures. This causes brittle client logic and unclear user errors. A unified guideline will reduce customer-side parsing bugs and make runtime fallback/rollout logic predictable.

Key proposals: 
- Canonical schema format: JSON Schema Draft-07 subset with explicit 'x-type-hint' extension for non-JSON native types (binary, timestamp, enum-casing). Keep the subset small to aid SDKs on embedded devices.
- Validation modes (per-route or per-call override):
  * strict: reject any type mismatch or unknown field. Returns HTTP 400/422 with detailed error list. Intended for admin/backend integrations.
  * permissive: coerce simple type mismatches (e.g., "42" => number) where safe; unknown fields are preserved in metadata. Returns 200 with warnings or 207 multi-status if partial.
  * coercive: aggressively coerce and normalize (trim strings, parse numbers/dates, flatten singletons). Used for front-end and 3rd-party integrations where UX matters.
- Error shape (stable across runtimes):
  * error.code: machine-readable short code (e.g., PARAM_TYPE_MISMATCH, PARAM_REQUIRED, PARAM_INVALID_ENUM, SCHEMA_DEPRECATION)
  * error.message: human-friendly explanation
  * error.path: json-pointer to offending field(s)
  * error.suggestion: optional actionable fix (e.g., "send 123 instead of \"123\"" or "use field 'user_email' instead of 'email' (deprecated)")
  * error.meta: optional string tags like "coercion_applied" or "deprecated_param"
- Backwards-compatible change rules: 
  * Safe additions: adding an optional field is always safe.
  * Deprecations: mark with 'deprecated' flag and provide 'replacement' hint. Deprecations run a 90-day telemetry window before removal for hosted tiers; Private deployments get advisory only.
  * Breaking changes: removing required fields or changing type is breaking and must be gated behind a versioned 'schema_version' with runtime rollout and automatic fallback to previous model variant.
- Mapping to HTTP semantics: 400 for syntactic/parse errors, 422 for semantic validation failures, 200 with warnings for permissive/coercive modes when server chooses to accept after normalization.
- Telemetry: emit structured event 'param_validation' with fields [route, schema_version, validation_mode, code, path, customer_id, model_variant] (aggregated for PII safety).

Format examples (authoring guidance): 
- Minimal number field: {
  "type": "number",
  "description": "timeout in seconds",
  "default": 30
}
- Enum with canonical casing (x-type-hint): {
  "type": "string",
  "enum": ["low","medium","high"],
  "x-type-hint": "lowercase-enum"
}
- Deprecated field: {
  "type": "string",
  "deprecated": true,
  "replacement": "user_email"
}

Acceptance criteria: 
1) Draft spec doc published to Confluence with concrete schema subset and examples.
2) Engine-level validation component implemented that accepts 'validation_mode' param and returns the proposed error shape.
3) SDKs (JS + Python) implement schema parser and basic coercion strategies.
4) Telemetry events emitted for validation failures in staging for at least two routes.

Risks/Tradeoffs: 
- Too many coercion rules can hide client bugs; prefer conservative coercion and explicit warnings.
- Private deployments may not want telemetry; must support opt-out.
- Versioning complexity if clients mix modes; require server-side 'schema_version' header in responses to aid clients.

Related artifacts: Confluence draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Function+Parameter+Contract+Draft (internal), PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/7812 (WIP), Design notes: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1xExampleDesignDoc/view
acceptance_criteria: 1) Publish Confluence doc and RFC. 2) Engine validation returns canonical error shape for a set of 10 representative schemas. 3) JS and Python SDKs ship support for schema hints and 'validation_mode'. 4) Telemetry shows <10% of production traffic hitting strict failures after rollout to two alpha customers.
